allowedScope.choice: Transform multimodal files into searchable representations, then ingest/index those representations with meaningful source metadata.
allowedScope.configuration: Use document/image/audio/video analyzers as appropriate; retain page/time/segment references; chunk and embed/index compatible content.
allowedScope.comparison: A Search index does not magically understand arbitrary raw audio/video; analysis outputs and retrieval representations must be explicit.
allowedScope.judgment: For a video knowledge base, store the transcript/segment description with timestamps and vectors so retrieved answers can point back to a segment.

allowedScope.choice: Choose keyword, vector, hybrid, and optional semantic ranking according to relevance requirements.
allowedScope.configuration: Match indexed/query embeddings; configure vector fields and semantic settings; preserve filters and avoid explicit sorting that replaces relevance.
allowedScope.comparison: Semantic ranking is not the same as creating embeddings; pure vectors can miss exact identifiers.
allowedScope.judgment: For product-code questions plus paraphrased symptoms, hybrid retrieval lets exact and conceptual evidence contribute before reranking.

allowedScope.choice: Use a skillset to enrich the document tree with OCR/layout/text features and map results into the index.
allowedScope.configuration: Set skill contexts and input/output paths; create normalized images for OCR; use outputFieldMappings for enriched nodes.
allowedScope.comparison: A successful skill computation can still yield an empty searchable field if mapping paths are wrong.
allowedScope.judgment: When OCR output exists in the enrichment tree but is absent from search results, inspect output mappings before re-running recognition.

allowedScope.choice: Combine readable document extraction/OCR, meaningful chunking, embeddings, and index projection for RAG.
allowedScope.configuration: Configure imageAction/normalized image paths, OCR/layout outputs, chunk source metadata, and embedding compatibility; inspect indexer failures.
allowedScope.comparison: OCR can create text without preserving document structure; layout-aware chunking may be needed for tables/sections.
allowedScope.judgment: A scanned manual should retain headings and page context so retrieved chunks do not separate warnings from the instructions they qualify.

allowedScope.configuration: Supply project connection/index, supported query_type and filters; use managed identity for private Search tool connections; retain citations.
allowedScope.comparison: Attaching a tool does not ingest missing documents or grant every downstream permission.
allowedScope.judgment: If an agent can query an empty or stale index, fix ingestion/index quality before changing the tool schema.

locators.heading: # Use function calling with Microsoft Foundry agents
locators.excerpt:
Microsoft Foundry agents support function calling, which lets you extend agents with custom capabilities. Define a function with its name, parameters, and description, and the agent's Foundry model can request your app to call it. Your app executes the function and returns the output. The agent then uses the result to continue the conversation with accurate, real-time data from your systems.

evidence.statement: Content Understanding provides separate document, image, audio, and video search analyzers; the document-search analyzer preserves layout and structured markdown for RAG.

locators.heading: ### Prebuilt analyzers
locators.excerpt:
- **RAG analyzers** - Optimized for retrieval-augmented generation scenarios with semantic analysis and markdown extraction. These analyzers return markdown and a one-paragraph `Summary`for each content item:
    - **`prebuilt-documentSearch`** - Extracts content from documents (PDF, images, Office documents) with layout preservation, table detection, figure analysis, and structured markdown output. Optimized for RAG scenarios.
    - **`prebuilt-imageSearch`** - Analyzes standalone images and returns a one-paragraph description of the image content. Optimized for image understanding and search scenarios. For images that contain text (including hand-written text), use `prebuilt-documentSearch`.
    - **`prebuilt-audioSearch`** - Transcribes audio content with speaker diarization, timing information, and conversation summaries. Supports multilingual transcription.
    - **`prebuilt-videoSearch`** - Analyzes video content with visual frame extraction, audio transcription, and structured summaries. Provides temporal alignment of visual and audio content and can return multiple segments per video.
- **Content extraction analyzers** - Focus on OCR and layout analysis (e.g., `prebuilt-read`, `prebuilt-layout`)
- **Base analyzers** - Fundamental content processing capabilities used as parent analyzers for custom analyzers (e.g., `prebuilt-document`, `prebuilt-image`, `prebuilt-audio`, `prebuilt-video`)
- **Domain-specific analyzers** - Preconfigured analyzers for common document categories including financial documents (invoices, receipts, bank statements), identity documents (passports, driver's licenses), tax forms, mortgage documents, and contracts
- **Utility analyzers** - Specialized tools for schema generation and field extraction (e.g., `prebuilt-documentFieldSchema`, `prebuilt-documentFields`)

locators.heading: # Hybrid search using vectors and full-text search in Azure AI Search
locators.excerpt:
- Runs full-text search and vector search in parallel.
- Merges results from each query by using [Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)](hybrid-search-ranking).

This article explains the concepts, benefits, and limitations of hybrid search. Links at the end provide usage instructions and next steps. You can also watch the embedded video for an explanation of how hybrid retrieval contributes to high-quality generative search applications.

locators.heading: ## Why use hybrid search?
locators.excerpt:
Hybrid search combines the strengths of vector search and keyword search. The advantage of vector search is finding information that's conceptually similar to your search query, even if there are no keyword matches in the inverted index. The advantage of keyword or full-text search is precision, with the ability to apply optional semantic ranking that improves the quality of the initial results. Some scenarios, such as querying over product codes, highly specialized jargon, dates, and people's names, perform better with keyword search because it can identify exact matches.

Benchmark testing on real-world and benchmark datasets indicates that hybrid retrieval with semantic ranker offers significant benefits in search relevance.

evidence.statement: Keyword retrieval can preserve exact names, identifiers, and specialized terms that pure similarity retrieval misses; combining it with vectors provides complementary relevance.

locators.heading: ## Indexer definition
locators.excerpt:
- ["fieldMappings"](search-indexer-field-mappings) map a source field to a search field.
- ["outputFieldMappings"](cognitive-search-output-field-mapping) map a node in an enriched document to a search field.

The "sourceFieldName" property specifies either a field in your data source or a node in an enrichment tree. The "targetFieldName" property specifies the search field in an index that receives the content.

locators.heading: # Document Layout skill
locators.needle: representation in Markdown or text format
locators.excerpt:
The **Document Layout** skill uses the [layout model](/en-us/azure/ai-services/document-intelligence/concept-layout) from Azure Document Intelligence in Foundry Tools to analyze a document, detect its structure and characteristics, and produce a syntactical representation in Markdown or text format. This skill supports text and image extraction, the latter of which includes location metadata that preserves image position within a document. Image proximity to related content is beneficial in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and [multimodal search](multimodal-search-overview) scenarios.

For transactions that exceed 20 documents per indexer per day, this skill requires you to [attach a billable Microsoft Foundry resource](cognitive-search-attach-cognitive-services) to your skillset. Execution of built-in skills is charged at the existing [Foundry Tools Standard price](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/cognitive-services/).
